business_problem: Royal Caribbean's guest journey was still largely analog - limited web visibility, a minimal app, printed daily newsletters and manual event signups - even as customers expected seamless digital experiences across a fleet that operated both onshore and at sea.
solution_summary: Royal Caribbean worked with EY Studio+ and EY technology teams to rebuild the cruise experience around a mobile, data-driven guest platform. The program started by reconfiguring legacy IT systems so the company could recognize each guest individually, authenticate them and personalize their itinerary across ship and shore. EY and Royal Caribbean then created a personalization engine that uses machine learning and analytics to learn guest preferences from boarding onward and recommend activities, food and services through the mobile app. The same digital stack added facial recognition for faster boarding, text notifications for luggage delivery, app-based activity booking and integrated automation that lets guests order from menus or alert crew to food sensitivities. Behind the scenes, the teams solved connectivity and orchestration challenges across fiber and satellite environments so the experience could run consistently across a multi-ship fleet.

solution_components.role: Speeds guest boarding by authenticating travelers as part of the digital journey.

solution_components.name: personalization engine
solution_components.role: Tracks preferences and orchestrates individualized recommendations and itinerary experiences.

solution_components.name: machine learning
solution_components.role: Learns from guest behavior to improve recommendations and personalized service actions.

solution_components.name: beacon technology
solution_components.role: Helps route app-based orders and location-aware service delivery to guests on board.

data_flow: Guests check in through the app and facial recognition, generating profile data that flows into the personalization engine. Machine learning uses behavior and itinerary signals to recommend activities, while integrated automation pushes notifications, orders and service requests to crews over the ship-and-shore connectivity layer.
business_outcome: Royal Caribbean turned digital guest interactions into a richer, lower-friction cruising experience that opens new revenue opportunities, gives guests more control over their trips and helps crews deliver more individualized service without relying on manual processes.
architecture_clues: The personalization engine sits on top of a rebuilt IT platform that recognizes guests as individuals and customizes itineraries.
The experience combines shipboard and shoreside connectivity across fiber and satellite links.
Integrated automation and beacon technology connect app activity to crew-side fulfillment.
Facial recognition, notifications and recommendations are all delivered through the same mobile experience.
